summary: This work demonstrates tunable Kerr and cubic nonlinearities in a superconducting NbTiN resonator hosting two aluminum-capped indium arsenide nanowire weak links, with independent flux and gate control over each junction. The authors achieve zero Kerr nonlinearity ($K/2\pi \approx 0$ kHz) while maintaining substantial cubic nonlinearity ($|g_3| \approx 35$–$70$ kHz), and experimentally demonstrate three-wave mixing parametric amplification with on-off gain exceeding 20 dB, reaching 25 dB in the optimized double-junction configuration.
motivation: Engineering resonators with nonzero cubic nonlinearity while suppressing detrimental Kerr nonlinearity is a central challenge for parametric amplification and bosonic-mode quantum control. Andreev bound states in tunable semiconducting weak links offer electrostatic and magnetic control beyond conventional Josephson junctions, but their nonlinear response had not been systematically characterized experimentally.
method: A double-junction Al-InAs nanowire weak-link device was embedded in an NbTiN resonator (bare frequency $\omega_r^0/2\pi = 6.759$ GHz, $Q_i^0 = 2.1 \times 10^4$, $Q_c^0 = 2.5 \times 10^3$). Kerr nonlinearity was extracted from power-dependent frequency shifts; cubic nonlinearity from three-wave mixing gain at $\omega_p = 2\omega_r$. An effective model based on Andreev bound state pairs ($U_{\mathrm{ABS}}(\varphi) = \pm\Delta\sqrt{1-\tau\sin^2(\varphi/2)}$) with gate-tunable transparency $\tau$ and phase $\varphi$ was used to interpret the results.
result: Kerr nonlinearity was tuned to zero (around $\varphi \approx 0.8\pi, 1.2\pi$ for datasets I and II) with cubic nonlinearity reaching $|g_3|/2\pi \approx 35$–$70$ kHz. The double-junction configuration achieved a maximum on-off gain of 25 dB with a $-1$ dB compression point at $-138$ dBm and $\approx 2$ MHz bandwidth. Two-tone spectroscopy confirmed Andreev bound state transitions, and the single-channel ABS model qualitatively captured observed $\delta\omega_r(\varphi)$, $K(\varphi)$, and $g_3(\varphi)$ trends across multiple gate configurations.
